claim: As the complexity of scientific inquiry increases, a single agent may struggle to manage an overwhelmingly large and diverse toolbox; hierarchical tool use in multi-agent systems can address this.
falsifier: One could compare the performance of a single agent versus a hierarchical multi-agent system on tasks requiring management of a large and diverse set of tools.

conditions: when the toolbox is overwhelmingly large and diverse
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported hypothesis and theoretical discussion; transfer beyond the described setting is unestablished.

title: Increasing complexity of scientific–single agent struggles boundary

claim: In a drug-disease similarity-based machine-learning prediction pipeline, a random forest classifier achieved higher predictive performance than logistic regression and support vector machine classifiers in cross-validation and retained strong performance on an unseen independent dataset.
falsifier: The relationship can be tested by applying random forest, logistic regression, and SVM classifiers to another drug-disease similarity dataset and comparing cross-validated and external AUC values under the same feature definitions.

conditions: Feature sets comprised four drug-drug similarity categories (chemical structure, side effects, gene ontology, targets) and three disease-disease similarity categories (phenotypes, human phenotype ontology, gene ontology)
Classification task was predicting drug-disease associations
Performance was assessed by cross-validation and external validation on an unseen independent dataset
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

claim: The decision problem of whether the Kleene star of a regular expression is not co-finite is in PSPACE.
falsifier: One can design a nondeterministic algorithm that uses polynomial space to decide co-finiteness of E* and verify its correctness via Savitch's theorem.

conditions: E is a regular expression over a finite alphabet
The decision is whether E* is not co-finite
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the formal setting and proof conditions reported in the source; transfer beyond this setting is unestablished.

title: Decision problem: given–problem is in PSPACE theorem

claim: A function f(x) can be estimated in polynomial time if and only if, for every given ϵ, there is a machine that produces an ϵ-approximation of f(t) in time polynomial in the input size and log ϵ⁻¹.
falsifier: The equivalence can be tested by constructing, for a given f, either a polynomial-time estimator or an ϵ-approximation machine and verifying the corresponding condition.

conditions: The machine is not necessarily solving a decision problem
The input size and the parameter ϵ are defined in the formal framework
The equivalence holds for functions f over the relevant real-number domain
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the formal framework for real-number computation in which this equivalence is proved; transfer beyond that framework is unestablished.

title: Polynomial-time estimation of functions–Existence of a machine theorem
